instruction: Browse FlightAware discussions and open the topic about flight tracking features.

metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to FlightAware discussions and opening the flight tracking category. Similar to the original task's navigation pattern but focuses on a specific topic category. Uses existing Chrome evaluator functions (get_active_tab_info and is_expected_active_tab) to verify the correct category URL is opened.
metadata.similarity_justification: Same website (FlightAware discussions), same interaction pattern (navigate discussions, find topic/category, open it), same difficulty level. Only difference is targeting a specific category instead of finding a topic by reply count.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses get_active_tab_info getter to extract active tab URL
Metric is_expected_active_tab with type='url' correctly compares actual URL against expected URL using compare_urls()

Expected URL https://discussions.flightaware.com/c/flight-tracking/6 is semantically correct - it points to the flight tracking category page which matches the instruction 'open the topic about flight tracking features'
Data flow is correct: getter extracts URL -> metric compares URL -> expected value matches instruction requirement
Evaluator provides complete coverage of the instruction requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor concern: get_active_tab_info reloads the page which could cause issues if the page has auth/cookies or redirects. However, FlightAware discussions is a public forum so this should work correctly in practice.

Consider whether the category page (/c/flight-tracking/6) is truly 'a topic' as the instruction says, or if it's a category containing topics. The current verification seems to treat 'topic about flight tracking features' as the category page itself, which is semantically reasonable but could be interpreted as requiring a specific discussion thread.
